intent: Hold the verified iteration 7 geometry (outer sensors x = ±0.03, y = 0.04, 15 mm spacing, 0.016 footprint, 0.18 m / 0.8 kg body, 0.12 m track, 0.03 m wheel radius) fixed. The race then tests the controller on the best-supported platform. Expected: a score at or near 160 with oval completions held. If the score falls well below 160 with oval completions lost, the controller change is the cause, not the geometry.
learning: Iteration 8 repeated iteration 7 and gave an identical 160.5, so the simulator is deterministic for a fixed design. The Integrator's feedback mislabels iteration 7 as ±0.036; the outcome table shows ±0.03 with kd 0.35. Under kd 0.35, ±0.03 beats ±0.036 (160.5 vs 97.7 at kd 0.25). Slalom line loss of about 1 is the remaining gap, and wheel_track 0.14 is the next single-variable test once the controller is settled.
rationale:
Iteration 7 (outer sensors at x = ±0.03, y = 0.04, 15 mm spacing, 0.016 footprint, 0.18 m / 0.8 kg body, 0.12 m track, kd 0.35) is the best raced result at 160.5. Iteration 8 repeated it and returned an identical 160.5, so the simulator is deterministic for this design. The oval completions (2 of 20, mean progress 0.81) drive most of the gain.

I am correcting the Integrator's reading of the outcome table. Their feedback says iteration 7 was raced at ±0.036 with kd 0.35. The table records iteration 7 at ±0.03. The ±0.036 layout was iteration 6 (kd 0.25, score 97.7). Under the same damping, pulling the outer pair in from ±0.036 to ±0.03 raised the score from 97.7 to 160.5, and slalom rms fell back toward the iteration 4 level. The evidence therefore favours ±0.03, and I am not reverting to ±0.036.

The body stays at 0.18 m / 0.8 kg (iteration 2 cut s-bend progress). The 0.016 footprint and y = 0.04 row stay (iterations 3 to 5 showed them neutral to slightly positive). Slalom line loss is still about 1 (1.05 in iteration 7), so the remaining untested geometry lever is wheel_track. I will not change it in this race, because the controller is also changing and the two effects would be confounded. I hold the verified 160.5 geometry fixed and plan wheel_track 0.14 as a single-variable test next iteration, if the controller holds.
